title: Dot product and its sign
body: $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=a_xb_x+a_yb_y+a_zb_z$. For nonzero inputs this also equals $|\mathbf a||\mathbf b|\cos\theta$. Positive, zero and negative distinguish acute, right and obtuse tail-to-tail angles. $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf a=|\mathbf a|^2$.
conditions: A dot product is a scalar. The component rule also allows zero inputs, although their angle is undefined.

title: Angle from components
conditions: Both vectors must be nonzero; use the angle between 0° and 180°. Keep the numerator's sign. Check the calculator's angle mode.

title: Signed component and vector projection
body: For $\mathbf b\ne\mathbf0$, $$s=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{|\mathbf b|},\qquad \mathbf p=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b}{\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf b}\mathbf b.$$ The scalar $s$ uses the direction of $\mathbf b$; $\mathbf p$ is the vector on its line. $|\mathbf p|=|s|$.
conditions: Both have the units of a. A signed component may be negative; its magnitude cannot. Do not substitute one output type for the other.

title: Cross-product meaning
body: In three dimensions, $\mathbf c=\mathbf a\times\mathbf b$ is a vector perpendicular to both inputs. For nonzero inputs, $$|\mathbf c|=|\mathbf a||\mathbf b|\sin\theta.$$ Order fixes direction by the right-hand rule.
conditions: Use a right-handed frame. $\mathbf b\times\mathbf a=-\mathbf a\times\mathbf b$. A zero result has no normal direction.

title: Why the projection multiplier works
body: Write $\mathbf p=c\mathbf b$ and require $(\mathbf a-c\mathbf b)\cdot\mathbf b=0$. This gives $c=(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b)/(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf b)$. The remainder is $\mathbf q=\mathbf a-\mathbf p$.
conditions: For nonzero b the denominator is positive, so the multiplier is unique. Reconstruction alone does not prove that q is perpendicular.

title: Checks with different purposes
body: For a projection, check p lies on b's line and $\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf b=0$. Also check $\mathbf p+\mathbf q=\mathbf a$. Then $|\mathbf a|^2=|\mathbf p|^2+|\mathbf q|^2$. For a cross product, check perpendicularity, scale and ordered orientation separately.
conditions: Both signs of a normal pass perpendicularity checks. Numerical tests support selected cases; they do not prove a general identity.

title: Zero and reversal
body: For nonzero inputs: dot zero means perpendicular; cross zero means parallel, including opposite directions. Replacing b by any nonzero multiple leaves the vector projection unchanged. A negative multiple reverses the signed component's sign.
conditions: Zero input a onto nonzero b gives zero projection. Zero reference b makes projection undefined. Never infer an angle from a zero input.

title: Area, normal and perpendicular distance
body: For adjacent edge vectors u and v, parallelogram area is $|\mathbf u\times\mathbf v|$; triangle area is half this. For a nonzero cross product, $\widehat{\mathbf n}=(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)/|\mathbf u\times\mathbf v|$. The distance of a's tip to b's line through the origin is $|\mathbf q|$.
conditions: Form edges from a common vertex. Length-edge products have area units; the unit normal is dimensionless. Swapping edges reverses the normal, not the area.

title: Ordered component rule
conditions: The cyclic order matters. For inputs in the $xy$-plane only $c_z$ can be nonzero, and the magnitude is $|c_z|$. Its sign records direction along the $z$-axis.

title: Supplied physical models
body: Constant-force work: $W=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf d$, with d the displacement of the force's application point. Torque about O: $\boldsymbol\tau_O=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F$, with r from O to that point. Its magnitude is $|\mathbf F|\ell$, where $\ell$ is the perpendicular lever arm.
conditions: Work model requires force constant in magnitude and direction. Torque must name the reference. Use J for work and N m for torque. Neither one force's work nor its torque alone determines the motion.

title: Units and input meanings
body: A product carries the product of its inputs' units. An angle ratio is dimensionless. A projection has the units of the vector projected, independent of the reference vector's scale. Position, displacement and perpendicular distance have different roles even when all are measured in metres.
conditions: Check both units and the quantity requested. Correct units cannot distinguish work from torque or a position from a displacement.

title: The small projection program
body: Use three numeric entries in x,y,z order; calculate bb, reject zero before division, calculate ab, then return each entry of b multiplied by ab/bb. Return None for a zero reference, not a zero vector. Compare ordinary, perpendicular, parallel and zero cases with hand predictions.
conditions: P101 notebook/list/condition/function readiness first. Our code assumes modest finite numeric inputs; it is not a general numerical library. Rounding discrepancies require interpretation, not automatic removal.
